In a road accident that took place on 12.03.2018, a certain Selladurai was was fatally knocked by a goods carrier bearing Regn.No.TN 46 M 3235 belonging to the first respondent and insured with the second respondent.
Selvadurai was riding a motor cycle bearing Regn.No.TN 46 L 5863 then.
Selvadurai was an agricultural coolie and was 42 years when he died and left behind surviving his widow and two young daughters.

sentences.text:
1 dependents of Selvadurai approached Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Principal District Court,
Perambalur with MCOP.No.386 of 2018.

entities.text:
Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Principal District Court,
Perambalur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2.For assessing compensation under the head of loss and dependency, the Tribunal reckoned the monthly income of the victim of the accident notionally at Rs.7,500/-, to which it added another 25% towards future prospects of increase in income and applied 14 as the multiplier and deducted 1/3rd towards the personal expenditure of the victim and arrived at a net value of compensation on this head at Rs.10.50 Lakhs.

After adding the compensation under other conventional heads, it arrived at a net value of compensation at Rs.10,80,000/-
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 3.Aggrieved by the inadequacy of compensation awarded, the daughters of the victim are before this Court.
It may be stated that the mother of these children, had died during the pendency of the claim petition before the Tribunal.

4.The learned counsel for the appellants made only two pointed statements; a) that the notional income as fixed by the Tribunal is unrealistically low; b) that the Tribunal has not fixed any compensation for loss of love and affection.

5.On careful consideration of the statement made by the learned counsel for the appellants, this Court deems it appropriate to fix Rs.10,000/- notionally as the monthly income of the victim, to which it adds another 25% towards future prospects of increase in income, applies 14 as the multiplier and deducts 1/3rd towards the personal expenditure of the victim and arrives at a net value of Rs.14,00,000/- as compensation for loss of dependency.
This Court retains the compensation awarded by the Tribunal towards the loss of estate and funeral expenses.
To this, this c o u r t a d d s a n o t h e r R s . 1 , 3 2 , 0 0 0 / - t o w a r d s l o s s o f l o v e a n d a f f e c t i o n f o r a l l https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis the three claimants.
Which implies, the total value of the compensation now determined is Rs.15,62,000/-.

The break-up is as below;
 Sl. Description Amount Amount Award  No awarded by awarded confirmed  Tribunal by this enhanced   (Rs) Court granted  (Rs)
Dependency -

2. Loss of Estate 15,000/- 15,000/- Confirme  3. Funeral Expenses 15,000/- 15,000/- Confirme  4. Loss of love and - 1,32,000/- -
 affection  10,80,000/- 15,62,000/ Enhanced by  Total - 4,82,000/-
Vidhya vs A.Dhanalakshmi on 13 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68365339/
2 6.In fine

, this appeal is partially allowed and the compensation payable is increased from Rs.10,80,000/- to Rs.15,62,000/-, together with interest at 7.5% per annum, from the date of petition till the date of deposit.

The second respondent/insurance company is now required to deposit the entire compensation amount with interest at 7.5%, less any amount already deposited,
within a period of six (6) weeks from the date of https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis receipt of a copy of this order.
The enhanced portion of the compensation is required to be apportioned in the same ratio in which the Tribunal has apportioned the compensation.
On such deposit, the appellants 1 and 3 are permitted to withdraw the award amount, now determined by this Court, along with interest and costs, less the amount if any, already withdrawn.

The compensation amount pertaining to the second appellant viz., Minor Elavarasi is directed to be deposited in a nationalised Bank in the interest bearing Fixed Deposit till the minor attains the age of majority and the natural guardian of the minor viz., Vidhya is permitted to withdraw the accrued interest on the deposit of the minor once in six months.
The appellants are directed to pay the necessary Court Fee, if any, on the enhanced award amount.
No costs.
13.12.2023 Tsg N.SESHASAYEE, J., Tsg https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis To 1.The
Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, The Principal District Judge, Perambalur.
